To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stress-induced intestinal barrier dysfunction leads to increased uptake of endogenous microbial products, which in turn activate immune cells and induce a proinflammatory state, which may lead to miscarriage.
stress-induced intestinal hyperpermeability and bacterial translocation is the key event that triggers the immune response in the context of pregnancy loss.

psychosocial stress enhances the intestinal permeability and bacterial translocation, which in turn results in an increased endotoxin load, which is a key mediator of pregnancy loss in the context of psychosocial stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the intestinal microfloral composition in stress-induced pregnancy failure.
the role of microbial endotoxin as a trigger of the stress response cascade and the potential role of probiotics in the prevention of pregnancy loss.
the role of stress-induced intestinal permeability and the impact of the intestinal microbiota on the stress-induced immune response and its consequences for pregnancy maintenance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intestinal flora and its products are important in the maintenance of pregnancy.
stress is associated with pregnancy loss, and that this is mediated, at least partially, by an increased intestinal permeability and subsequent bacterial uptake.
the intestinal flora may be a novel target in stress management and may contribute to a better understanding of spontaneous abortion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intestinal microfloria is the 'gut' of the whole stress response cascade.
psychosocial stress induces a proinflammatory response in the mother, which in turn affects the fetus.
the intestinal flora is a crucial component in the regulation of pregnancy maintenance and the prevention of miscarriages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gut is the gatekeeper of the immune system, which can be influenced and manipulated by probiotic bacteria, and this has a direct influence on pregnancy outcome and the stress response.

the stress response is a complex cascade of events, involving the intestinal flora and its products as a major player in the immune response, and that the gut is not only the gateway to the body but also a major source of endogenous danger signals.
the intestinal microfloral composition and the integrity of the intestinal barrier function are important factors to be considered in future research on the role of stress in pregnancy maintenance.
